findings.title: Reject repeated continuations before offering another scan action
findings.persona: Reader looking for a sparse late match, including keyboard and assistive-technology users
findings.confidence: high for the stated returned-cursor premises; occurrence against the real owner is unverified
findings.source_evidence: The seen check runs only while checkedPages < 4. On the fourth page the returned nextCursor is not compared with seen before result is returned. The chapter consumer also follows pages.hasNextPage blindly; searchPagesOptions.getNextPageParam returns page.next without comparing prior pageParams. Deduplication prevents duplicate cards but does not refuse stalled traversal.

instances.relationship: unchanged shared continuation dependency newly consumed here

reproduction_or_required_assertion: Resource scan: return four empty incomplete pages for inputs null, A, B, C with nextCursor A, B, C, A respectively. Every response passes checkedPage immediate-progress checks. The fourth output must be refused rather than rendering another link to already-seen A; current source returns ok:true. Also cover a cycle at the action boundary.

Chapter continuation: first page next=A; subsequent successful page returns the same opaque A and no new matchUnit. Assert refusal/restart and no further repeated requests, including a two-token cycle. Current source performs up to four duplicate requests per action and continues to offer Check more. Keep already loaded chapters.
findings.minimum_follow_up: Existing Discover/search continuation owner adds progression checks in its current boundary, with exact opaque-token equality and bounded behavior assertions; preserve typed refusal and existing dedup/scan tests. Do not decode or invent tokens.

findings.title: Keep chapter focus recovery active through retry and restart
findings.persona: Keyboard or screen-reader reader recovering a failed later chapter page
findings.confidence: high for bypassed focus path; resulting browser/AT focus requires execution
findings.source_evidence: Failure clears scan at lines 95-97. Try again calls fetchNextPage/refetch directly without creating another scan, and restart also clears scan before refetch. The only first-new-link/end-summary focus code is in the effect guarded by scan. When recovery succeeds the focused recovery button disappears without that focus handoff. RetryPreservesChapters asserts visibility and cursor, not focus; its retained final screenshot has no new-link focus outline.

findings.title: Validate the quoted query before Exact phrase navigation
findings.persona: Reader refining a valid long query without losing active conditions
findings.confidence: high; independent of unproved keyword/exact matching semantics
findings.source_evidence: The enabled Exact phrase button wraps state.q in two quotation marks and navigates without validating the resulting length. parseBrowseState rejects more than 80 Unicode code points. A valid unquoted 79- or 80-code-point query becomes 81 or 82, so the local edit leads to the bad-link surface instead of a valid scoped search.
reproduction_or_required_assertion: Direct-load a valid 79-code-point unquoted q with realm/language/type/topic/exclusion conditions; activate Exact phrase. Require either an in-place actionable validation message preserving the task or a valid admitted destination. Current handler pushes an 81-code-point q rejected by the parser. Cover 78/79/80 code-point boundaries and Unicode without changing the approved owner query semantics.
findings.minimum_follow_up: Existing selection-controls owner validates the proposed q before pushing, preserving current input/conditions and explaining any bound. Extend its boundary coverage; do not claim that quote toggling proves native exact/keyword semantics.
